text.p: Polish debt-ridden construction company Espebepe SA wants its largest creditors to write off 80 percent of its debts instead of the earlier proposed 95-percent write-off, Espebepe said in a statement late on Tuesday.
Creditors are expected to decide on the deal on May 16, after two previous meetings on March 14 and April 14 failed to reach conclusive decisions on the fate of the company.
Espebepe, which has 75-million-zloty debts, wants one fourth of the remaining debt to be paid in 14 quarterly payments and three fourths after that.
It said, however, that rather than paying back the debts directly it would seek to offer a debt-for-equity scheme if the deal is approved.
Espebepe earlier said its shareholders would vote on a new share issue increasing its share capital by 20 percent on May 31.
Espebepe said the deal would be approved if creditors representing 80 percent of its liabilities voted in favour.

It said that according to the offer smaller creditors, to which the company owes less than 7,500 zlotys, would write off 20 percent of the debts. The remaining debt would be paid by the end of the third quarter of 1997.

Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA (PBKS), Espebepe's largest creditor, earlier said it wanted to write off 40 percent of its debts and to change the remainder into convertible bonds, but Edspebepe rejected the proposal as unrealistic.
Espebepe had a net loss of 52.1 million zlotys in 1996 and 2.6 million in the first quarter of 1997.
